decompositions.new: p-9707d6ff step 100000 (~/commute-data/artifacts/qwen3-1.7b-p-9707d6ff-torch), trained on chat text at 2,048 tokens, 30% Qwen3-1.7B's own responses (some thinking)

row_sets.T: the 128 FineWeb rows of experiments/qwen_adversary/results/tokens.json (512 tokens each)
row_sets.G: the first 128 GSM8K test prompts (chat template, the GSM8K baseline's INSTRUCTION, thinking off) followed by Qwen3-1.7B's own greedy response, cut at 512 tokens in all (results/rows.json, written once by stage 1)
row_sets.G-think: the same prompts with thinking on, cut at 512 tokens in all

numbers.ci_kl: per row: mean over the row's positions of KL(target || masked) with m = g, delta off (nats); then the mean over the 128 rows, rows equal-weighted
numbers.active: per row: mean over positions of the count of subcomponents with g > 0.1, summed over the 196 sites; then the mean over rows
numbers.adv_kl: the config's evaluation adversary (PGDReconLoss: one U(0,1) source per site shared by all rows and positions plus one delta scalar, 20 sign steps of 0.1 up the token-weighted mean KL over the row set, clipped to [0,1], one random start, torch generator seed 0, the same for both decompositions); per row: mean over positions of KL(target || masked) at the final sources; then the mean over rows, rows equal-weighted

references.old_T_adv_kl: 1.70 for seed 0 (1.62 the mean of seeds 0-2), experiments/qwen_adversary on an H100; this run uses seed 0 only
references.new_chat_ci_kl: about 0.17 (bundle README, held-out chat text at 2,048 tokens, during training)

rule.ratio: mean over rows of the new decomposition's per-row value / the same mean for the old decomposition, on the same rows (paired)
rule.interval: row bootstrap: 10,000 resamples of the 128 row indices with replacement (numpy default_rng seed 0), the same indices for both decompositions; the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles (linear interpolation) of the resampled ratios
rule.pass: ratio < 1 and the interval's upper end < 1 (strict; a tie at 1 is a miss)
rule.unreadable: fewer than 2 rows, unequal row counts, a non-finite per-row value, or a zero old mean in the data or in any resample

P1.claim: the new decomposition is more faithful with its own CI on GSM8K text, thinking off

P2.claim: the new decomposition is more faithful under the adversary on GSM8K text, thinking off

P3.claim: the same as P1 with thinking on

P4.claim: the same as P2 with thinking on

predictions.basis: the plan's Expected line: new trained on chat text with 30% Qwen3-1.7B's own responses, old on firestock3 at 512 tokens
predictions.reported_without_prediction: T for all three numbers; the active count on every row set (its ratio is computed, no verdict)

controls.a_recon: V U of the new decomposition reproduces each of the 196 HF matrices: max relative Frobenius error <= 0.0055 (the bundle's reconstruction_check.csv bound); the largest gap to the csv's per-site values is reported
controls.b_jax: torch Gamma (bf16) of the new decomposition on the JAX library's own 29 taps (param-decomp 7d2e5aee8, experiments/qwen_new_decomp/jax_reference.py) vs the JAX g on the 8 rows of experiments/qwen_port/results/tokens.json: share of (position, subcomponent) pairs with |g_torch - g_jax| > 0.1 at most 1e-4 (old port's same check: 2.4e-5); end to end, active counts and the CI-masked KL beside JAX's are reported
controls.c_old: the old decomposition through this code: mean ci_kl on T within 2% of the stored 0.141670617449563 (|mean / 0.14167 - 1| <= 0.02)
controls.if_any_fails: stage 0 prints STAGE 0 FAILED and the job exits 1 before stage 1; the measure stages refuse to start

edge_cases_checked: tests/test_qwen_new_decomp.py runs the rule on: a tie (ratio exactly 1: miss), an interval upper end at exactly 1 (miss), a zero old mean (unreadable), an old mean that is zero only in some resamples (unreadable), a single row (unreadable), unequal row counts (unreadable), a NaN value (unreadable), a missing decomposition (unreadable), and the do-nothing state (new = old row for row: ratio 1, miss). The do-nothing state cannot pass: the rule needs the ratio strictly below 1.
